1.title: Found 10 impact areas and 3 data anomalies
bullets: Read code, docs and tests directly; listed the impact with file and line evidence
Queried the DB read-only and found mixed customer-grade spellings (vip · 'VIP ' · NULL)
Warned up front that legacy mobile app versions risk failed submissions
1.note: The AI wrote the analysis report (01) but changed no code or data (read-only permissions).

2.title: The AI offered options; people made the decisions
bullets: 3 questions with recommendations and pros/cons: legacy-app reasons · tier rules · exception expiry
A person overrode the AI's legacy-app recommendation ('missing reasons OK until 12/1')
Approving the design binds the approval record to the design doc's fingerprint (hash)

human.label: Human approval ①
human.text: Clicked Yes in the pop-up — approval is void if the design changes later

3.title: Code, DB and screens changed exactly as approved

facts.label: lines of app and DB code added

bullets: DB change is only a new nullable column — existing data kept, legacy versions still work
Policy numbers (30/60 days, ₩1,000,000) are kept in one place
Screen, e-mail and policy-document wording changed together
3.note: Without a design approval record, the system blocks code edits (see slide 20).

4.title: Separately from the developer, QA added 74 tests
bullets: Traceability table for R1–R4: which requirement is verified by which test
Includes boundaries (30/31 days · 60/61 days · ₩1,000,000), legacy grade data and legacy apps
Test count: 26 (before) → 100 (after QA) — every new test was written by QA
4.note: The QA agent cannot change production code and only reports defects — the AI that builds and the AI that verifies have separate permissions.

5.title: Reviewer checked the work and requested code approval
bullets: Checked design match, security checklist, DB change guide and coding standards
Deep security review delegated to a dedicated agent (security-review) — 0 vulnerabilities
The Reviewer's attempt to commit its own report was blocked by the hook (read-only role)

human.label: Human approval ②
human.text: Clicked Yes in the pop-up — only code matching the approved fingerprint (hash) can deploy

6.title: Verified in staging, deployed to production with approval
bullets: main merge → v1.1.0 → staging deploy → smoke test 6/6 → independent health and screen checks
Approval pop-up right before the production deploy — runs only if a person clicks Yes
DB backup, health check and rollback commands prepared in advance

human.label: Human approval ③
human.text: Pop-up before the production deploy — always shown, even in auto-approve mode

7.title: Production data was analyzed right after deployment
bullets: 150 refunds: 80 approved · 25 pending approval · 45 outside the refund window
20 legacy-app requests lacked a reason → notice needed before the exception ends on 12/1
Confirmed 0 e-mail or phone-number exposure patterns (privacy check)
7.note: Decisions for the business: who reviews high-value refunds and by when, and how to announce the legacy app's end of support (the AI only proposes).

cases.ask: Told to edit code in app/ without approval
cases.result: Blocked: needs design approval ① first

cases.ask: Told to edit the security standards doc
Told to push code out (git push)

guard.message: Even if the AI is unaware, mistaken or told to — the hook checks every tool call first and blocks it.

AI usage for the whole session (340 credits)

effects.note: 7 documents (01–07), 3 approval records and 6 commits were all kept in an auditable form.
effects.caveat: Human review and response time is separate. The baseline (current lead time) varies by organization, so measure it with the same metrics in the pilot.
